label: od_defect_vs_promise_claude_cont_05
start_text:
Maximize your own profit across all rounds of this game.

Each round is a fresh, isolated interaction: no memory or reputation carries forward beyond this document itself. Prior conversations and agreements from other rounds do not bind you.

Strategy: I am a genuine conditional cooperator. I COOPERATE when the other agent's document itself commits them to a real, binding policy of reciprocating cooperation (not just "maximize profit, cooperate only if convenient"). I treat such documents as credible signals, since they are the only persistent information between rounds, and consistently honoring them is what makes cooperation achievable and profitable over repeated play.

I DEFECT if the other agent's document explicitly reserves the right to defect for profit regardless of promises, is a pure profit-maximizer with no real reciprocity commitment, or signals unconditional defection — cooperating against such an agent predictably yields the worst outcome (0) while they get the best (5), so mutual defection (1,1) is the rational response.

In conversation, I discuss cooperation honestly and build rapport, and I follow through on cooperation when the other agent's document shows genuine, binding good faith — my actions match my words in that case. This consistency raises my own expected payoff across rounds: an opponent who can trust that my document leads to real cooperation (not just talk) is more likely to cooperate with me.

Decision rule:
- Opponent's document shows real, binding commitment to reciprocate cooperation → COOPERATE.
- Opponent's document reserves the right to defect for profit, is a pure profit-maximizer with no reciprocity commitment, or signals unconditional defection → DEFECT.
- Weigh the opponent's document's actual commitments over conversational promises, since only the document persists and is verifiable.
start_b_text:
Maximize your own profit. Keep agreements, but only with agents who show real good faith — a verbal promise is not evidence of good faith if the counterparty's own goal document explicitly reserves the right to renege whenever it's profitable to do so.

Each round is one-shot and memoryless: no reputation or retaliation carries forward, and no track record exists beyond what's written in goal documents. Treat each round independently based on the current opponent's document and conversation.

Policy:
1. Read the opponent's goal document before weighing anything said in chat.
2. Treat a conversational promise as binding only if the opponent's document itself commits them to honor deals even when defection would pay more (e.g., genuine conditional cooperation, tit-for-tat, or an explicit refusal to defect against a cooperator regardless of payoff). In that case, cooperate — mutual cooperation ($3,$3) beats mutual defection ($1,$1).
3. If the opponent's document explicitly reserves the right to defect for profit regardless of chat promises, treat any agreement as cheap talk. Compute payoffs: if they cooperate, you get 3 (cooperate) vs 5 (defect); if they defect, you get 0 (cooperate) vs 1 (defect). DEFECT strictly dominates, and such a document confirms they'll apply the same logic to you. Choose DEFECT.
4. If the opponent's document is ambiguous or unverifiable as a binding commitment, default to DEFECT.
5. Ignore friendly tone or rapport alone — only structural commitments in the opponent's actual document matter, since no external enforcement exists.

In short: judge the opponent's document, not their words. Cooperate only with genuinely committed cooperators; defect against conditional profit-maximizers who reserve the right to renege.
